headline: GR SILVER EXTENDS SAN MARCIAL 150m PAST MRE BOUNDARY: 21.9m @ 168 g/t Ag INCL. 6.15m @ 447 g/t Ag IN NEW SE AREA (TSXV:GRSL)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / GR Silver Mining Corp.
snippet: GR Silver Mining Corp. (TSXV: GRSL) reported July 10 that diamond drill hole SMS26-07 at the San Marcial silver project in Sinaloa, Mexico intersected 21.9 metres at 168 g/t silver — including 6.15 metres at 447 g/t silver in the SE Extension target area — confirming that high-grade silver mineralisation continues for at least 150 metres southeast of the 2023 NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate boundary. The SE Extension was not previously included in any resource model; SMS26-07 is the first drill-confirmed intersection in this ground, validating the geological projection that the structural corridor hosting the known resource extends further to the south. GR Silver's active 20,000-metre 2026 step-out campaign has already produced the company's best-ever single-hole result earlier this year (45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag including 8.25m at 8,579 g/t Ag in SMS26-04); the July 10 result adds a new lateral vector to the resource expansion picture. San Marcial is a low-sulphidation epithermal system in one of Mexico's most historically productive silver districts — 150 metres of confirmed SE extension at grades averaging 168 g/t, open in multiple directions, is the systematic step-out work that converts a defined resource into a substantially larger one ahead of an updated resource estimate.

headline: HONG KONG LAUNCHES GOLD CLEARING SYSTEM TO CHALLENGE LBMA — HAU PRICE TICKER, YUAN SETTLEMENT, SOVEREIGN ALTERNATIVE TO LONDON
snippet: The Hong Kong Precious Metals Central Clearing Company (HKPMCC) inaugurated its gold-clearing system on July 7, 2026 — a direct structural challenge to the London Bullion Market Association's decades-long dominance of global gold price discovery, settlement, and physical delivery. The system introduces a HAU price ticker, enables yuan-denominated settlement linked directly to the Shanghai Gold Exchange, and offers tax incentives and expanded vault capacity to attract institutional participants. The strategic architecture is explicit: it gives sovereign central banks, Asian commercial banks, and large institutional gold buyers a clearing venue that routes outside London and New York — reducing exposure to the settlement risk and potential asset-freeze liability that made dollar-denominated clearing a political liability after Russia's frozen reserves in 2022. For junior mining investors, this is the most consequential structural shift in global bullion market infrastructure in decades. A sovereign-backed alternative clearing venue in Asia deepens and broadens the buyer base for physical gold, potentially strips COMEX paper-positioning pressure from spot prices during periods of elevated short interest, and accelerates the institutional de-dollarisation of gold that central bank buying has driven since 2022. Every gold-producing project that sells metal into a genuinely global market — not just a London-priced one — benefits from the depth this infrastructure adds.

headline: FORTUNA Q2: 72,217 GEO ON GUIDANCE TRACK AS SÉGUÉLA EXPANSION VOTE LOOMS — DIAMBA SUD FS: $1B NPV, 60% IRR AT $3,500 GOLD (NYSE:FSM)
snippet: Fortuna Mining Corp. (NYSE: FSM, TSX: FVI) reported July 9 that Q2 2026 gold equivalent production reached 72,217 ounces across its four operating mines — steady versus Q2 2025 (71,229 GEO) and Q1 2026 (72,872 GEO), with H1 of 145,089 GEO tracking the midpoint of full-year guidance of 281,000–305,000 GEO. The larger catalysts are two development decisions now on the immediate horizon: Fortuna's Board will decide in coming weeks whether to approve an expansion of the Séguéla gold mine in Côte d'Ivoire to 2.3 million tonnes per annum, following Lycopodium engineering studies completed in late June; and the Diamba Sud gold project in Burkina Faso has received its Environmental and Social Impact Assessment approval and published a feasibility study delivering an after-tax NPV5% of US$1.0 billion at a $3,500 gold price, an IRR of 60%, and a one-year payback period. Both catalysts land while gold trades at $4,100+ — approximately 17% above the Diamba Sud FS gold price, meaning the published NPV materially understates the project's value at spot. Fortuna's Q2 production report is the operational baseline; the Séguéla expansion approval and Diamba Sud construction decision are the equity events that will define the company's next 12–18 months.

headline: SILVER X PERU Q2 RECORD: 380k AgEq oz PROCESSED +50% QoQ AS NUEVA RECUPERADA HITS 750 t/d DESIGN CAPACITY (TSXV:AGX)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Silver X Mining Corp.
snippet: Silver X Mining Corp. (TSXV: AGX) reported July 9 that Q2 2026 production at its 100%-owned Nueva Recuperada silver mine in Peru reached a record 380,436 silver equivalent ounces processed — up 50% quarter-on-quarter from Q1 2026 — with 283,029 AgEq ounces produced, up 57% QoQ and 57% year-over-year. The operational milestone: the Nueva Recuperada plant averaged 684 tonnes per day through Q2, with April specifically reaching 751 tonnes per day — the plant's nominal 750 tpd design capacity achieved for the first time. Year-to-date production of 634,000 AgEq processed and 463,000 produced is consistent with the company's stated path toward approximately 6 million AgEq ounces annually by 2029. Silver X represents a rare species among TSXV-listed silver producers: an operating mine with confirmed design-capacity throughput, a multi-year production growth roadmap, and a defined resource base at one of Peru's most mineralised polymetallic belts. The transition from ramp risk to steady-state execution — confirmed by April's 751 tpd benchmark — changes the risk framework for investors assessing the company's path to scale. At $59/oz silver, that framework matters.

headline: SILVERCO DRILLS 1,100 g/t Ag OVER 10.3m AT CUSI — 25m FROM PLANNED STOPES, OUTSIDE MINE PLAN, Q4 2026 RESTART MOBILIZING (TSXV:SICO)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Silverco Mining Ltd.
snippet: Silverco Mining Ltd. (TSXV: SICO) reported July 8 underground drill results from its 100%-owned Cusi silver mine in Chihuahua, Mexico — including 10.3 metres grading 1,100 g/t silver from zones located just 25 metres from planned near-term development stopes and entirely outside the existing mine plan resource model. The practical significance is immediate: this high-grade interval is adjacent to first-year production areas, was not previously modelled in the restart mine plan, and represents incremental high-grade material that improves expected head grade for the restart quarter. Silverco is executing a 30,000-metre 2026 program combining infill, expansion, and exploration across multiple vein zones at Cusi; two local mining contractors have begun mobilisation toward a planned Q4 2026 restart targeting initial concentrate output before year-end and full operational capacity by mid-2027. At $59/oz silver, high-grade underground silver operations entering production are structurally rare — concentrate demand is firm, and Cusi's 1,100 g/t intervals adjacent to development add a quality dimension to what was already a defined restart thesis. The restart case does not depend on new discovery; it is being reinforced by drilling that adds material outside the existing plan.

headline: ISOENERGY HURRICANE SOUTH HITS 43,160 cps — ALL 4 SUMMER HOLES ANOMALOUS, 48.6 Mlb ATHABASCA RESOURCE SHOWING EXPANSION (ISOU)
snippet: IsoEnergy Ltd. (NYSEAMERICAN: ISOU) reported July 8 that summer drilling has resumed at the Hurricane South Trend within the Larocque East project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, following a temporary suspension due to nearby wildfires, with four of a planned 20 holes completed and all four intersecting anomalous radioactivity. The strongest interval: 11,075 counts per second (cps) over 3.5 metres, including a peak spike of 43,160 cps over 0.5 metres. Hurricane carries a Mineral Resource of 48.6 million pounds of U3O8 at an average indicated grade of 34.5% — one of the highest-grade uranium resources anywhere in the Athabasca Basin — with 2.7 Mlb at 2.2% Inferred. The summer program's focus on the Hurricane South Trend targets expansion of this resource along the corridor's southern extension, where the winter 2026 program already extended mineralisation 540 metres along strike via a newly identified fault zone returning 30,050 cps. With uranium trading above $85/lb and four consecutive summer holes intersecting anomalous radioactivity, the data pattern reinforces the thesis that Hurricane has material additional pounds to add to the current resource before any development decision. The full 20-hole, 8,000-metre program has 16 holes remaining.

headline: TRAXYS: LITHIUM FLIPS FROM GLUT TO SCARCITY ON ASIAN DEMAND — AI DATA CENTERS + ENERGY STORAGE BUILD DEMAND FLOOR BEYOND EVS
snippet: One of the world's largest commodity trading firms, Traxys, is calling a lithium market inflection: what began 2026 as a structurally oversupplied market — with CATL's Jianxiawo mine resuming, lithium carbonate falling to 151,750 CNY per tonne, and multiple Australian projects restarting — is now showing supply-deficit signals on 'very healthy Asian demand and an under-supplied market.' The structural mechanism behind the demand surprise: accelerating Chinese government procurement of battery energy storage systems to power AI data centers and manage industrial grid loads has created a demand channel entirely independent of EV sales — which collapsed 25% in North America after the elimination of U.S. EV tax credits but remain positive year-over-year in China. The implication for market structure: three simultaneous supply restarts (CATL Jianxiawo, Mineral Resources Bald Hill, Core Lithium Finniss) are being absorbed by a demand base that has grown faster than the supply response. For junior lithium explorers holding advanced-stage projects, the Traxys call matters because it identifies the recovery driver as demand-led rather than supply-curtailment-led — a structural distinction that produces more durable price support. The AI data center grid storage demand channel is likely persistent regardless of short-term EV sentiment, providing a floor that wasn't present in the 2024–2025 lithium trough.

headline: ROSLAND CAPITAL FILES CHAPTER 11: $49M IN UNFILLED ORDERS — GOLD DEALER DESTROYED BY RISING PRICES, STRUCTURALLY SHORT ITS OWN METAL
snippet: Rosland Capital LLC, the Los Angeles precious metals dealer whose television campaigns promoted gold as a haven from market turmoil, filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition on July 2, 2026 — a court-supervised liquidation, not a reorganisation, with $1–10 million in assets against $50–100 million in liabilities and a self-declared capital deficit exceeding $60 million. The mechanism of collapse is the investor lesson: Rosland operated an order-lag model that left it structurally short the metal it sold, accepting customer payments before sourcing the underlying gold. As gold rose from $1,500/oz in 2023 to $4,300 at end-2025 and peaked at $5,620 in January 2026, the company's $49 million in deferred revenue — customer orders accepted but not yet filled — became a catastrophic unhedged short position. By June 2026, 470+ customer voicemails, emails, and formal complaints had been routed through compliance, and at least one customer had already filed suit. Money Metals Exchange's July 6 analysis delivers the operative takeaway for retail investors using physical gold for wealth preservation: allocated, segregated storage with independently audited custodianship is the only structure that fully eliminates counterparty risk. Unallocated accounts, storage programs run within dealer operations, and pre-funded unfilled orders represent implicit counterparty exposure to the dealer's financial health — Rosland's collapse has now quantified that exposure at $49 million in potential client losses.

headline: EKATI FACES JULY 28 CCAA DEADLINE — 74% DIAMOND PRICE COLLAPSE, 200+ CREDITORS, CANADA'S OLDEST DIAMOND MINE IN COURT SALE PROCESS
snippet: Arctic Canadian Diamond Company Ltd. (ACDC), operator of the Ekati diamond mine in Canada's Northwest Territories and a subsidiary of ASX-listed Burgundy Diamond Mines Limited, is operating under CCAA protection with a court-supervised sale and investment solicitation process now underway and a stay of proceedings extended until July 28, 2026. Canada's first diamond mine, opened in 1998, now faces more than 200 creditors with approximately $340 million in secured debt — the federal government is the largest secured creditor — and $93.3 million in unsecured claims that receive proceeds only if the sale generates value above secured claims. The structural cause is a 74% collapse in natural diamond prices from their post-COVID peak, driven by simultaneous scaling of laboratory-grown diamond production to industrial volumes and a Chinese consumer retrenchment that eliminated the world's fastest-growing diamond market. For mining investors, the Ekati CCAA is a textbook case study in commodity substitution risk: the same forces that destroyed natural diamond economics — cheaper synthetic alternatives at scale, demand destruction in the key growth market — represent the ultimate tail risk for any mined commodity facing technological disruption. Whether a qualified buyer emerges before July 28 will determine whether Canada's diamond mining sector retains critical processing and workforce infrastructure or faces permanent closure of its oldest producing mine.

headline: H2 2026 PRECIOUS METALS RECOVERY: MINERS TRADE 25-30% BELOW JAN PEAK AS GOLD HOLDS $4,100 — 3 STOCKS FOR THE REBOUND
snippet: An Investing.com analysis distributed via Globe and Mail and Yahoo Finance identifies a compressed setup in precious metals equities heading into H2 2026: gold has partially recovered from its January $5,300 peak to the $4,100–$4,200 range, but major gold and silver miners remain 25–30% below their January 2026 highs despite sustaining near-record operating margins. The structural argument: Newmont (NEM) trades approximately 44% below consensus analyst price targets at roughly 12x earnings — a historic discount to both its own valuation history and the S&P 500 multiple — while silver royalty companies like Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) benefit from a silver market in its sixth consecutive structural supply deficit with potential for an industrial demand re-acceleration as energy storage procurement scales. The technical case for a late-July through August recovery rests on the July 14 CPI print: a sub-3.8% reading collapses September rate-hike probability, removes the primary headwind suppressing gold below $4,200, and creates the institutional catalyst for reallocation into hard-asset equities from treasury positions. The gold equity bull case — record sector unit profits estimated at $2,787/oz for Q2, record central bank buying of 474 tonnes in Q1 2026, structural mine supply constraints — has not changed. Only the timing of when Western institutional capital decides to close the NAV discount remains the open question, and the July 14 CPI is the first scheduled opportunity to reset the odds.
